$comment: Hand-edited properties; geometry rebuilt from trace.json by make past (decision 12).

properties.name: Port Costa to Benicia, the train ferry

sources.note: "At Port Costa extensive wharves were built, and a ferry established to transfer freight and passenger trains across" to Benicia; the line to Suisun opened December 28, 1879.
The bridge "was opened to regular train service on October 15" and "will take the place of the train ferry service which has handled freight and passenger trains across Carquinez Straits since 1879".

properties.notes: The ferries Solano (1879) and Contra Costa (1914) carried whole trains across the Carquinez Strait. The crossing is drawn as the shortest path over water between the slips, as the 1898 Karquines sheet places them.
properties.geometry_method: The shortest path over today's water from -122.18370,38.04600 to -122.16485,38.04465 (1822 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1 land and water), kept off the shore: the sources give the terminals, not the course. Port Costa's slip read off the 1898 Karquines sheet; Benicia's at the end of the waterfront track.

properties.name: Benicia, the ferry slip to the line near Army Point

sources.note: Labelled Southern Pacific, along Benicia's waterfront.

properties.notes: From the slip along Benicia's waterfront to the main line, which today's track joins near Army Point. Trains to Sacramento left it for the bridge in 1930; when it last carried passengers isn't sourced.
properties.geometry_method: OpenHistoricalMap way 200464960 (CC0, as of 2026-10-15), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS Napa CA 1902 topographic map, cut to -122.12801,38.04760; checked on USGS Karquines 1:62,500 (1898) and USGS Benicia 1:24,000 (1952). Cut where it meets today's track near Army Point. OpenHistoricalMap's way was traced from the 1902 Napa sheet (1:125,000); on the 1952 sheet it lies along the waterfront track.
